page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.large is a burstable virtual machine instance within the shared family, built on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, provisioning 2 vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core with 2 threads. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. It includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage, and does not include dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements reflect the burstable allocation model and single-core physical topology. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 2229.6 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1493.0, placing its compute throughput in lower performance tiers relative to dedicated compute profiles. Memory read throughput over large blocks measures 16.3 GB/sec, while write operations reach 14.44 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates static web serving throughput of 1.48 GB/sec and Redis SET throughput of 2.54 million operations per second, with small-model LLM inference producing 23.72 text generation tokens per second.

From an infrastructure perspective, ecs.t5-c1m4.large prioritizes resource economy over sustained multi-threaded compute capacity. The inclusion of 8.0 GB of RAM provides adequate memory headroom for basic multitasking, but the burstable CPU credit model restricts performance under continuous heavy compute stress. The lack of included local storage and public IPv4 addresses requires relying on external cloud attachments for persistence and external routing.

The ecs.t5-c1m4.large server type is suited for low-utilization workloads that experience intermittent compute requirements. Suitable deployments include lightweight internal web servers, staging and testing environments, microservices, small relational database testing, and basic background cron task workers.
